structured_output.hypothesis: In measured stature by age, girls' and boys' height-velocity curves across roughly ages 6 to 18 have similar shape, but the girls' adolescent acceleration starts, peaks and ends earlier than the boys', and the two curves differ in peak amplitude.
structured_output.pass_criterion: All of the following hold. (1) Smoothed height-velocity curves (cm/yr) are computed from sex-specific, survey-weighted mean height by exam age in months, using pooled NHANES cycles and ages 6 to 18. The age at peak velocity is earlier in girls than in boys by at least 1.0 year, and the 95% bootstrap CI (at least 1000 resamples) of the boys-minus-girls difference excludes 0. (2) The age at which velocity rises above its prepubertal minimum (onset) and the age at which it falls back to near the minimum (end) are each earlier in girls than in boys. (3) The curves are similar in shape: the Pearson correlation between the girls' curve and the boys' curve shifted by the estimated phase difference is at least 0.85, and it is higher than the unshifted correlation. (4) Peak amplitudes differ, with a bootstrap CI for the amplitude difference that excludes 0.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any of these holds. The boys-minus-girls difference in peak-velocity age is below 0.5 years, or its 95% bootstrap CI includes 0. Girls' onset or end is not earlier than boys'. The phase-shifted correlation is below 0.7, or the shifted correlation is not higher than the unshifted one, which would mean the shapes are not similar. The amplitude difference CI includes 0, which would mean no amplitude difference.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'curve of growth velocity' is annual height increment (cm/yr) against age. 'Phase' is timing along the age axis: onset, peak and end of the adolescent spurt. 'Amplitude' is peak velocity. The NHANES data are cross-sectional, not longitudinal. Velocity is therefore estimated by differencing smoothed (spline or LOESS) weighted mean height-for-age curves. This captures the average timing of the spurt but blurs individual peaks, so amplitudes are biased downward. Phase is the primary test and amplitude is secondary. Measured stature (BMXHT) is used, and age is exam age in months (RIDAGEEX). Sex is RIAGENDR and weights are the MEC exam weights (WTMEC2YR).

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES records measured standing height (BMXHT in the Body Measures files) for children and adolescents. The Demographics files give sex (RIAGENDR), exam age in months (RIDAGEEX) and MEC exam weights. Pooling several cycles gives enough sample per age-month bin to estimate sex-specific height-by-age curves and their derivative. Both sexes are measured, not self-reported, and the data are free to download as XPT files.
